title: Apply Bitwise Operations to Make Strings Equal
description:
You are given two 0-indexed binary strings s and target of the same length n. You can do the following operation on s any number of times:
For example, if s = "0110", you can choose i = 0 and j = 2, then simultaneously replace s[0] with (s[0] OR s[2] = 0 OR 1 = 1), and s[2] with (s[0] XOR s[2] = 0 XOR 1 = 1), so we will have s = "1110".
Return true if you can make the string s equal to target, or false otherwise.

Constraints:
constraints: s and target consist of only the digits 0 and 1.

examples.text:
Input: s = "1010", target = "0110"
Output: true
Explanation: We can do the following operations:
- Choose i = 2 and j = 0. We have now s = "0010".
- Choose i = 2 and j = 1. We have now s = "0110".
Since we can make s equal to target, we return true.

Input: s = "11", target = "00"
Output: false
Explanation: It is not possible to make s equal to target with any number of operations.

hints: Think of when it is impossible to convert the string to the target.
If exactly one of the strings is having all 0’s, then it is impossible. And it is possible in all other cases. Why is that true?
